entities.summary: Ceslaus Odrowąż, O.P., was born in Kamień Śląski in 1184, the son of the noble Odrowąż family, and relative to the influential Hyacinth of Poland. A member of the Polish nobility, Ceslaus dedicated his life to the service of the Catholic Church, becoming a respected figure in the Polish clergy. His dedication to the Church led to his appointment as a bishop, a position he held until his death in 1242. Ceslaus's legacy as a devoted servant of the Church has endured, with his name remaining a testament to the enduring influence of the Catholic faith in Poland. The statue of Ceslaus Odrowąż in Kamień Śląski's cathedral remains a symbol of his enduring devotion to the Church. Throughout his life, Ceslaus's actions were guided by his strong faith, which he expressed through his tireless work in promoting the Catholic Church's teachings and institutions. His commitment to the Church's values has had a lasting impact on the religious and cultural landscape of Poland.
